title: Google PageBreak AI Agent Finds Over 500 XSS Vulnerabilities Across Its Web Applications
key_facts: Google's Product Security team disclosed PageBreak, an internal AI security agent.
It found and validated more than 500 cross-site scripting (XSS) flaws across Google's first-party web applications.
Each candidate flaw goes to a validator that tries to reproduce the exploit on a running application; only proven ones are reported, giving a near-zero false-positive rate per Google.
It began as a pilot in November 2025 and became a full project in January 2026; most deployments use Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 3.5 Flash.
As of 4 Sep 2026 it found only two XSS issues across hundreds of apps built on Google's hardened web frameworks, both in internal or debug endpoints.
Google found no evidence of exploitation in the wild for the cache-poisoning example.
Google is linking PageBreak to CodeMender, which proposes fixes for human review.
quote_evidence: The AI proposes an attack path; deterministic tooling proves whether the path actually works.
Google said it found no evidence of exploitation in the wild.
why_it_matters_hint: AI used on the defensive side with proof-based validation.
event_date: Disclosure date not stated; data as of 4 Sep 2026
notes: Company's own claim about itself, relayed by GBHackers; Google original not read; disclosure date unknown.
